requirements.issuer: National Institute of Standards and Technology
requirements.source_access_notes: Official NIST AI RMF 1.0 January 2023 PDF accessed substantively on 2026-10-01; printed Core pages 22–33. AI-authored comparison, not human verification.
requirements.requirement_summary: Organizations applying the NIST AI RMF should ensure that their evaluations of AI systems involving human subjects meet requirements applicable to those evaluations, including protection of human subjects.
applicable_actor: Organization applying the NIST AI RMF, through AI actors responsible for evaluations involving human subjects
governed_object: AI-system evaluations involving human subjects: applicable requirements, including human-subject protection
requirements.governance_expectation: Organizations applying the NIST AI RMF should ensure that their evaluations of AI systems involving human subjects meet requirements applicable to those evaluations, including protection of human subjects.
applicability_conditions: Applied voluntarily and contextually according to the organization's AI risks, resources and risk tolerance.
The evaluation of the AI system involves human subjects.
exceptions_or_qualifications: The NIST AI RMF is voluntary, non-sector-specific and use-case agnostic; outcomes are applied contextually rather than as a mandatory checklist.
Framework use augments existing risk practices and does not displace applicable laws, regulations and norms.

interpretation_provenance.source_analysis_method: AI-authored semantic coherence review against MEASURE 2.2 and MEASURE 2 context; independently assessable evaluation dimension with inherited actor, subject and trigger. No FC relationship or occurrence finding inferred.

review_limitations: AI-authored source comparison and independently allocated metadata; no human review or verification.
The subcategory does not enumerate specific human-subject protection rules or prescribe sampling methods, sample sizes or demographic quotas.
